conditions: The identity is the named Xerox MPL language line, grounded in the printed MPL(B) representation.
limitations: This does not identify the design and runtime artifacts in the full historical catalog as language versions, prove actual compatibility, or collapse the MPS system, Mesa, MPL(A), and MPL(B).

triggers: A newly available original, corrected catalog entry, archive byte change, or contrary edition and implementation evidence.

statement: The Xerox PARC text printed February 25, 1974 identifies MPL(B) as an interim programming language for MAXC and the PDP-10, extending MPL(A) in limited ways and referring to later MPL versions. It identifies the Xerox MPL language line through its explicitly named version.
